The Watershed Remote Sensing Lab is based in the [Department of Geography, Earth and Environmental Sciences](https://www.unbc.ca/department-geography-earth-and-environmental-sciences) at UNBC, in Prince George, British Columbia. We work at the intersection of watershed hydrology, cryospheric science, remote sensing and environmental sensor design.

## Graduate students

Prospective graduate students [**(Master's only at this time)**]{.underline} interested in these themes are welcome to get in touch. Graduate work in the lab is normally through the [Natural Resources and Environmental Studies (NRES)](https://www.unbc.ca/graduate-programs/natural-resources-environmental-studies) program at UNBC.

When you reach out, please include a short description of your research interests and why they fit the lab and your CV, highlighting any relevant fieldwork, programming or geospatial experience.

**Graduate projects [could]{.underline} include the following themes (these are themes, not research questions):**

- *Remote sensing in watershed science*

  - Advancing the use of lidar in hydrology

  - Testing new satellite sensors for hydrological applications

  - Thermal remote sensing of stream and lake temperature, from drones and from space, including remote-sensing-driven estimates of water temperature

- *Open, low-cost monitoring*

  - Democratizing hydrometric monitoring with open-source software

  - Developing low-cost, DIY, automated water samplers to understand water quality

  - Extending the [RemoteLogger](https://watershed-rs.shinyapps.io/remotelogger/) platforms

- *Hydrology of northern BC*

  - Progress towards a nested physical hydrological model for northern BC

  - The thermal regime of permafrost in northern BC and its impact on hydrology

  - Assessing the impact of glacier change on future water resources in northern BC

  - Extending the [watershedBC](https://watershed-rs.shinyapps.io/watershedBC/) platforms

Students are also welcome to propose their own project within these themes — if your interests overlap with the lab's work, get in touch.

## Undergraduate students

Undergraduate research assistant positions come up through the academic year and over the summer, including [NSERC Undergraduate Student Research Awards (USRA)](https://nserc-crsng.canada.ca/en/funding-opportunity/undergraduate-student-research-awards). Current and past assistants are listed on the [People](people.qmd) page. Get in touch if you would like to be considered.

## Professional mentorship

I mentor articling agrologists through the [BC Institute of Agrology](https://bcia.com/) Professional Agrologist Mentorship Program. Current and past mentees are listed on the [People](people.qmd) page.
